gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-inscriptional-p: Gugi's lowercase climbs nearly to the capitals, with open-cut terminals and curves that match its stems exactly. Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian is its softer foil, with big open eyes on every e and a, and a deep middle band.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-jp: Gugi draws its n arches as thick as the stems beside them, which gives the display heading a blunt, confident look. And Noto Sans JP, a plain sans with a very high x-height, would feel thin if the heading were made small.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Gugi holds a technical-pen steadiness throughout, its terminals cut open so the counters flow outward. But Noto Sans Khmer, a sans-serif with chisel-notch openings and small letters standing almost capital-sized, makes a long paragraph feel generous.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Gugi keeps its curves and stems in lockstep, with lowercase that nearly reaches the capitals in height. And Noto Sans Khojki gives that firmness somewhere to rest, its wide exits passing light through and a large eye on every e.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-lao: A line width that never swells or tapers defines Gugi, with open-cut terminals on its lowercase. Noto Sans Lao does the quieter work, pushing its x-height well above the usual while keeping c, e, and a mouths open.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Gugi runs a single track width like a neon sign tube, with terminals cut open on every curve. Noto Sans Limbu sits beside it looking friendlier, its gaping curves and lofty small letters easing off the heading's rigidity.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Loud, uniform, and sharply cut, Gugi hums along as one soft, featureless line with its lowercase rising near the capitals. Noto Sans Lisu settles beneath it, wide-open s curves and tiny ascender gaps.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-mahajani: Bold and distinctive, Gugi cuts stems and curves from one gauge of tubing. Noto Sans Mahajani, a plain sans whose lowercase stands high against the capitals and whose e has a funnel-wide throat, is the pair's best quality: it keeps the heading's strength readable.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-marchen: Rope-fine strokes laid into letter shapes give Gugi a distinct, bold look. And Noto Sans Marchen, a sans-serif with curves ending in clear daylight, would look oversized if its capital-sized small letters were set large.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-mayan-numerals: Cut ribbon of constant width, that's Gugi, bold and unmistakable. It does display punch best, while Noto Sans Mayan Numerals does the quieter job, with high-bodied small letters and a visibly gaping c at any size.
